raw_response:
I will do this year much like I did last year, just a little tighter on money and labor because there are only 2 of us at home. On my 34.5 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the surest way for me to get grain, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton. I do not like to gamble with a big change. If the neighbors around me use a seed and I see the stand is even and the ears or bolls come well, I will follow that. For fertilizer, I would rather put a little extra than watch the crop turn pale and lose yield. With well water in hand, I can push wheat at the key watering times, give maize 2 good irrigations if the rain is short, and keep cotton from drying out when it is setting squares and bolls. Since I have 34.5 mu, I also have to think about work: wheat and maize are easier to run across bigger land, while cotton takes more watching, more spraying, and more hand work, so I will not plant too much cotton. I will plough for cotton land, and on the wheat-maize land I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is faster and cheaper for me.
